papers.abstract: Recent experiments have revealed unexpected mirror-symmetry breakings in the charge density-wave (CDW) state of rare-earth tritellurides, suggesting a putative ferro-axial CDW state. Here we report polarization-resolved Raman scattering measurements tracking the point-group symmetry breakings across the CDW phase transition in the rare-earth tritelluride ErTe$_3$. We show that the mirror-symmetry breakings follow closely the emergence of the CDW order, suggesting a single component CDW order parameter. Furthermore, Raman measurements in the $A_{2g}$ symmetry channel above the CDW transition temperature indicate the absence of significant ferro-axial fluctuations. We discuss the broad implications of these findings with respect to the nature of the CDW state in the tritellurides.

papers.abstract: Bloch point singularities play an important role in magnetic systems, mediating changes in topology in three dimensional configurations. However, until now they have only been observed as isolated objects or as part of individual topological textures. Here we present the experimental observation of a 1D dipole chain of Bloch points in an anisotropic chiral magnet using soft X-ray magnetic vector tomography. We identify that the chain of Bloch point singularities lies along a boundary between regions of opposite chirality and that neighbouring Bloch and anti-Bloch points are stable at separations down to 60 nm. The stability of the Bloch points is determined to be closely related to the surrounding topology of the magnetisation configuration and a threshold separation for the spontaneous annihilation of Bloch point-anti-Bloch point pairs within chiral domain walls is identified to be approximately 90 nm in distance. This observation of a chain of Bloch points and the insight into their stability, offers a route to explore the correlative behaviour of such topological point defects. The behaviour and control of such point defects is of relevance for the control of 3D magnetisation configurations, and provides a new route towards the creation of correlated configurations of singularities in a magnetic system.

papers.abstract: Crystal symmetry governs the physical properties of materials and provides the framework for interpreting their microscopic excitations and macroscopic responses. In altermagnets, the crystal symmetries that relate opposite-spin sublattices give rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting despite compensated magnetization. Determining the real crystal symmetry is therefore essential for understanding the intrinsic electronic and magnetic properties. For the altermagnetic semiconductor $α$-MnTe, conflicting Raman assignments have left both its intrinsic lattice excitations and its crystal symmetry unresolved. Here we combine high-resolution Raman and second-harmonic generation (SHG) spectroscopy with first-principles calculations to distinguish intrinsic lattice excitations from Te-derived spectral contributions and to examine bulk inversion symmetry of $α$-MnTe. We show that several prominent Raman features previously assigned to $α$-MnTe instead originate from segregated Te clusters or precipitates. The remaining intrinsic Raman response consists of a single Raman-active mode assigned to the calculated $E_{2g}$ phonon, consistent with the centrosymmetric $D_{6h}$ symmetry. The SHG response agrees with surface electric-dipole and bulk electric-quadrupole contributions expected for a centrosymmetric $D_{6h}$ crystal, supporting the preservation of bulk inversion symmetry in $α$-MnTe. Our findings revise the Raman assignments in $α$-MnTe and provide a basis for interpreting its altermagnetic properties within the appropriate crystal-symmetry framework.

papers.title: Lattice Symmetry Remnants in Spatial and Temporal Entanglement of Quantum Critical Spin Chains
papers.summary_en: The paper shows how microscopic lattice symmetries and an LSM constraint leave observable signatures in spatial and temporal entanglement at criticality, constraining how the infrared CFT is realized at its boundary.
papers.summary: Quantum critical lattice models carry universal information beyond the bulk data of their infrared conformal field theory (CFT): microscopic lattice symmetries constrain how the CFT is realized. papers.abstract: Quantum critical lattice models carry universal information beyond the bulk data of their infrared conformal field theory (CFT): microscopic lattice symmetries constrain how the CFT is realized. We probe these remnants through the spatial and temporal entanglement of two Euclidean-evolved states from the same critical model. In the finite-length scaling regime, a conformal boundary encodes the long-distance effect of the short-range initial state, and boundary CFT (BCFT) organizes the universal low-lying entanglement spectrum. We formulate the temporal state as a uniform infinite matrix product state evolved by a symmetry-preserving infinite matrix product operator, using a local factorization regular even at arbitrarily small Trotter steps. For the Ising and three-state Potts chains, whose relevant symmetries are onsite, the spatial and temporal constructions approach the same BCFT structure; varying the initial state engineers conformal boundaries distinguishable spectroscopically. The spin-1/2 XXZ chain instead realizes a Lieb--Schultz--Mattis (LSM) constraint between internal U(1) symmetry and one-site translation. A U(1)-preserving short-range spatial state accommodates it through a doubled unit cell and inequivalent entanglement cuts, whereas the temporal state remains uniform along Euclidean time. Successive spatial transfer steps pump the temporal entanglement spectrum between translation-related Dirichlet sectors, equivalently between integer and half-integer compact-boson zero modes. Breaking U(1) removes both the zero mode and the alternation. Continued evolution at fixed bond dimension crosses over from the finite-length BCFT regime to a finite-entanglement regime generated by symmetry-allowed relevant deformations. Thus microscopic symmetry and anomaly data remain visible in universal entanglement by constraining the boundary realization of the infrared CFT.

papers.relevance_reason: This theoretical study shows how microscopic lattice symmetries and the LSM constraint shape entanglement spectra in quantum-critical spin chains.
papers.summary_zh: 本文展示了微观晶格对称性及 LSM 约束如何在临界系统的空间与时间纠缠中留下可观测特征，并限制红外共形场论在边界处的实现方式。

In the XXZ chain, the U(1)-translation LSM constraint is accommodated spatially by a doubled unit cell and inequivalent cuts, whereas successive spatial transfer steps pump the temporal entanglement spectrum between translation-related Dirichlet sectors, corresponding to integer and half-integer compact-boson zero modes. Breaking U(1) removes both the zero mode and the alternation; at fixed bond dimension, continued evolution crosses from the finite-length BCFT regime to a finite-entanglement regime generated by symmetry-allowed relevant deformations.

papers.title: Magnonic time crystal with lasing coherence
papers.authors: Jiantao Song, C. K. Wei, Shuhuan Ma, Yiming Pan, Zhijian Chen, Li Yu, Wei Lu, Bimu Yao
papers.summary_en: The authors report a room-temperature magnonic time crystal in yttrium iron garnet that emits radiation with lasing coherence. The work connects driven magnon interactions to subharmonic temporal order, coherent emission, and nonlinear reservoir-computing features.
papers.summary: Discrete time crystals (DTC) can respond at an integer multiple of the drive period. papers.abstract: Discrete time crystals (DTC) can respond at an integer multiple of the drive period. Internal order-parameter measurements have advanced studies of this novel non-equilibrium phase of matter; however, turning this order into highly coherent, externally accessible radiation remains challenging: pump-driven nonlinear processes must supply sufficient gain to compensate dissipation while preserving subharmonic stability. Here we realize a room-temperature magnonic time crystal (MTC) with radiation of lasing coherence using a pump-induced magnon mode in yttrium iron garnet. A microwave beat drive produces robust period doubling over a finite parameter range, with spectral signatures of higher-order MTC at stronger driving. The emitted field exhibits linewidth narrowing to 260.0 Hz and a first-order correlation decay time of $995 μs$. Our model links this response to three-magnon confluence, yields a stability region consistent with experiment and predicts a possible transition to chaos. We further map the complex temporal dynamics into frequency-resolved nonlinear features for reservoir computing. These results bridge time-crystalline order and nonlinear information processing through intrinsic magnon-magnon interactions and lasing coherence.
papers.physics_advance: A room-temperature magnonic time crystal emits radiation with lasing coherence, and its period-doubled response is linked to three-magnon confluence.
papers.relevance_reason: The experiment reveals coherent nonequilibrium magnetic order and its nonlinear dynamics in a solid-state magnon system.

papers.title: Multifractal Magnons Around Localized Defects
papers.authors: Adarsh Hullahalli, Yusuf Khand, Christos Panagopoulos, Christina Psaroudaki
papers.summary_en: The authors show that localized defects, including spin defects and skyrmions, can generate mesoscopic multifractal magnon wavefunctions in otherwise crystalline two-dimensional magnets without disorder or quasiperiodicity. They propose that skyrmion-induced hybridization with magnetically active internal deformation modes could make a subset of these states observable using uniform ac fields.
papers.summary: Multifractal wavefunctions fluctuate over a hierarchy of spatial scales, remaining spatially extended while exhibiting strongly nonuniform structure. We show that magnons in otherwise crystalline two-dimensional magnets can exhibit such behavior on mesoscopic scales, without disorder or quasiperiodicity. A localized defect can mix discrete groups of nearly degenerate magnon states in a finite samp
papers.abstract: Multifractal wavefunctions fluctuate over a hierarchy of spatial scales, remaining spatially extended while exhibiting strongly nonuniform structure. We show that magnons in otherwise crystalline two-dimensional magnets can exhibit such behavior on mesoscopic scales, without disorder or quasiperiodicity. A localized defect can mix discrete groups of nearly degenerate magnon states in a finite sample, generating multiscale interference patterns and multifractal wavefunctions. We demonstrate this mechanism for both a simple spin defect and topological magnetic skyrmions. Large-scale spin-wave calculations for skyrmions in chiral and frustrated magnets reveal clear multifractal diagnostics over the full accessible range of system sizes of above-gap modes. Crucially, skyrmions make these states experimentally observable by hybridizing them with magnetically active internal deformation modes, which gives a subset of the multifractal states a nonzero magnetic dipole moment. These states can therefore be excited by uniform ac fields and remain distinguishable at realistic frequency resolution, providing a direct route to observing mesoscopic magnon multifractality.

papers.abstract: Spin reorientation near room temperature offers a route to controlling antiferromagnetic order, yet LaFeO$3$, which lacks a magnetic rare-earth ion, is generally expected to retain its spin orientation along the $a$ axis below $T{\mathrm N}\approx740$~K. Here, we investigate LaFe$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$O$_3$ ($x=0$ and 0.1) using temperature-dependent magnetization and Raman spectroscopy over 200--400~K. Both compositions exhibit magnetic anomalies at 285.6 and 323~K, respectively, accompanied by correlated deviations of 12 Raman modes from their conventional anharmonic behavior. Principal component analysis and a global fitting approach reveal a common temperature-dependent phonon response, with mode-dependent amplitudes and signs. To interpret these anomalies, we develop a Landau-based spin-phonon coupling model describing complete, partial re-entrant, and incipient spin reorientation. Comparison with the experimental Raman profiles favors a partial, re-entrant rotation of the N'eel vector in both compositions, centered near 290~K. Ni substitution narrows the characteristic reorientation interval from approximately 116 to 84~K and enhances the magnetization anomaly by a factor of four. An additional feature near 262~K in LaFeO$_3$ is consistent with the Morin transition of trace $α$-Fe$_2$O$_3$. These findings suggest that partial spin reorientation can emerge without magnetic rare-earth ions and establish collective Raman phonon anomalies as a sensitive indirect probe of magnetic anisotropy changes in orthoferrites.

papers.abstract: Understanding the microscopic origin of magnetic damping is essential for describing magnetization dynamics in nanoscale magnetic systems. In this work, we develop a microscopic framework to derive Gilbert damping terms from specific interactions in ferromagnetic conductors and magnetic insulators. In ferromagnetic conductors, magnetic damping is dominated by the s d exchange interaction between the localized magnetic moments and the itinerant electrons, which is effectively equivalent to an electronmagnon interaction. From the spin diffusion equation and the spin transfer torque therein, we obtain the corresponding quantum LLG equation. In magnetic insulators, where free electrons are absent, spin phonon interactions become the primary source of the damping.Starting from an effective spin phonon interaction and using linear response theory, we derive a quantum LLG equation with a Gilbert damping tensor analytically. Our results demonstrate that different microscopic interactions lead to qualitatively different structures of magnetic damping. Instead of being described by a universal scalar parameter, Gilbert damping can exhibit spatial dependence and tensorial characteristics determined by the underlying microscopic interactions.

papers.abstract: The partially disordered (PD) phase, in which magnetically ordered and Kondo-screened sites coexist, has been proposed as a possible ground state of geometrically frustrated heavy-fermion systems. We investigate its dynamical properties in the half-filled periodic Anderson model on a triangular lattice by calculating the dynamical spin susceptibility within the random-phase approximation built on a self-consistent Hartree-Fock solution. We show that successive quantum phase transitions from the Kondo-insulating phase to the PD phase and to a magnetically ordered phase are driven by the condensation of triplon modes originating predominantly from the Kondo-screened sites. In the PD phase, magnons and triplons coexist and hybridize, leading to characteristic level repulsion in the excitation spectrum. These results reveal how triplet excitations evolve into collective magnetic modes across the successive phase transitions and highlight the dynamical interplay between magnetic order and Kondo screening in frustrated heavy-fermion systems.

papers.title: First- and Second-Order Electron Position Correlators Reveal Topological Phase Transitions
papers.authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Christian Loer Llemit, Massimo Capone
papers.summary_en: The authors propose characterizing topological phase transitions using spatial and temporal two-point correlators of fluctuations in the electronic position operator. They show that the correlators’ antisymmetric sector yields the Chern number in a coincident limit and that higher-order Chern–Chern correlators capture criticality in nonperiodic or genuinely dynamical settings.
papers.summary: The theory of conventional critical phenomena is built around the concepts of fluctuations and correlators of local observables. papers.abstract: The theory of conventional critical phenomena is built around the concepts of fluctuations and correlators of local observables. Here, we show that topological phase transitions can also be characterized through spatial and temporal two-point correlation functions associated with fluctuations of the electronic position operator. The key object is the antisymmetric part of the position-position correlation function, which yields the Chern number in the equal-time and equal-space limit. When the system is translationally invariant in space or time (the latter case corresponding to an equilibrium condition), these two-point correlators reduce to one-variable functions of the remaining variable. Remarkably, these functions are both reminiscent of critical behaviour, including divergent correlation times and lengths signalling the phase transitions. Away from these conditions, namely in non-periodic systems or genuinely dynamical processes, criticality is instead better captured by higher-order Chern-Chern correlators constructed from local or dynamical markers obtained as coincident-point limits of the position correlators. These higher-order Chern-Chern correlators can be seen as double Levi-Civita contractions of second-order position correlators, selecting the antisymmetric sector in each index pair. We substantiate this framework through numerical simulations and analytic calculations. Our results establish a general correlator-based description of topological phase transitions, applicable to crystalline, noncrystalline, equilibrium, and dynamical systems.

papers.abstract: The square-lattice compass model is a paradigm of bond-dependent frustration, yet experimental evidence for its characteristic spin correlations has remained elusive. Here we identify compass correlations in the square-lattice intermetallic ErRu$_2$Si$_2$ using single-crystal neutron diffuse scattering. Comparative measurements on the isostructural compounds NdRu$_2$Si$_2$ and ErRu$_2$Si$_2$ reveal a pronounced contrast between nearly uniform diffuse rings in the former and strong intensity modulation between Brillouin zones in the latter. Through the magnetic neutron polarization factor, this modulation reveals compass correlations that couple moment orientation to the correlation wavevector. Crystal-field spectroscopy identifies four preferred in-plane orientations for the Er$^{3+}$ moments. A minimal compass-Heisenberg model incorporating this anisotropy quantitatively reproduces the diffuse scattering and accounts for the double-$Q$ vortex-antivortex ground state. Fits with the compass couplings fixed at values set by the dipolar energy scale retain good agreement with the data, supporting a substantial dipolar contribution to the bond-dependent interactions. Our results establish a square-lattice platform for compass physics and suggest that dipolar interactions, acting together with local crystal-field anisotropy, can shape directional magnetic correlations alongside conduction-electron-mediated exchange.

papers.abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) provide a controllable platform for engineering topological Andreev spectra. At zero temperature, Andreev bound states (ABSs) with nonzero Chern numbers give rise to quantized transconductance between superconducting terminals. We derive the finite-temperature transconductance of MTJJs using linear-response theory. We first demonstrate the destructive role of temperature: changes in the thermal occupations of the ABSs destroy exact transconductance quantization. We then show that finite temperature can also play a constructive role by making the transconductance sensitive to finite-energy topological crossings hidden from the zero-temperature response. Our results establish the thermal limitations of transconductance quantization and identify finite-temperature transport as a probe of otherwise inaccessible topology in Andreev spectra.

papers.abstract: Charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity have long been recognized as competing orders. However, recent achievements establish that the interplay between these two collective electronic phenomena can be more perplexing, with emergent phenomena arising from their cooperation. Here we report a distinctive case of the kagome superconductors CsV3Sb5-xSnx, in which the characteristics of superconductivity evolve in accordance with the form of CDW order. As the triple-Q CDW in CsV3Sb5 transforms to a short-range stripelike CDW at xc = 0.07, a sudden change in superconducting properties occurs concomitantly. A combination of thermodynamic, electrical transport and scanning tunneling microscopy experiments reveals a heterogeneous superconducting state beyond xc: the superconducting gap exhibits pronounced spatial variation, in conformity with a distribution of critical temperature and the resulted superconducting precursor effects. Moreover, abundant normal fluid persists deep into the superconducting state, as evidenced by remnants of electronic specific heat and zero-energy quasiparticle interference. These observations are unrelated to the chemical inhomogeneity and residual strain effect introduced by Sn substitution. Instead, they emulate the phenomenology that a sign-changing superconducting order parameter is subject to strong pair-breaking scattering with the short-range charge stripes and hence reflect the unconventional nature of superconductivity developing inside the charge-stripe state.

papers.abstract: Manipulating flux quanta in topological superconductors is central to vortex braiding in quantum computing. Their interferometric superconducting rings can host either topologically protected edge states with fluxes confined inside the central hollow area or vortex bound states in flux cores at the annulus walls. Here we demonstrate a strategy to drive topological edge states into vortex bound states by tuning the relative scale of vortex size and annulus width in nano-ring interferometric device on 2M-WS$_2$ topological superconductor. Near its superconducting transition where the coherence length exceeds the annulus width, Little-Parks oscillations exhibit expected periods for flux bundles in ring-center, consistent with edge states residing at inner and outer rims of the annulus. Upon cooling, where the coherence length shrinks below the annulus width, the unexpectedly increased oscillation period reflects multiple fluxes distributed along annulus region in flux necklace configuration, implying a transition from extended edge states to localized vortex bound states. Ginzburg-Landau simulations and local density-of-states calculations with Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations reveal that large values for both Ginzburg-Landau parameter and flux-pinning energy are vital for such a transition. Our findings provide a novel strategy for understanding flux manipulation towards flux braiding and topological quantum computing.

papers.abstract: The emergence of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at the so-called magic angle reveals a range of intriguing phases, such as superconductivity and Mott insulating states, resulting from electrons entering a correlated state. This establishes twisted bilayer graphene as an excellent platform for exploring correlation effects in many-body phases and across various twist angles. However, in most cases, the twist angle is not an easy parameter to control because it exhibits structural instabilities such as relaxation and reconstruction that reduce the correlation effects. Here, we report the unexpected appearance of a flat band at the \bar{M} point far from the Fermi level in a 2.4° twisted bilayer graphene, directly visualized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. Our work is the first observation of flat bands away from the \bar{K} point in twisted bilayer graphene and highlights the need to probe the entire Brillouin zone to fully capture electronic states in twisted structures.

The effective magnetization due to temporal fluctuations of the assosciated dipoles couple to an external magnetic field resulting the magnetoelectric term $\mathbf{H} \cdot (\mathbf{P}
papers.abstract: We propose a microscopic theory of the phonon-mediated thermal Hall effect in quantum paraelectrics, driven by the intrinsic paramagnetism due to quantum fluctuations of the (nearly) critical optical phonon modes. The effective magnetization due to temporal fluctuations of the assosciated dipoles couple to an external magnetic field resulting the magnetoelectric term $\mathbf{H} \cdot (\mathbf{P} \times \dot{\mathbf{P}})$ in the effective Lagrangian density of the polarisation field $\mathbf{P}$. This coupling splits the transverse optical phonon spectrum into right- and left-circularly polarized chiral branches. Using the chiral phonon Green's functions and the Kubo formalism, we derive the thermal Hall conductivity $κ_{xy}$ from the heat-current correlation function. We observe that $κ_{xy}$ is proportional to the difference in spectral weights of the two chiral modes, $κ_{xy} \propto A_+^2 - A_-^2$, establishing a direct microscopic link between phonon chirality and transverse heat transport. Our theory predicts three key observations: (i) a linear-in-magnetic-field response $κ_{xy} \propto H$ at low fields, evolving into nonlinear behavior at higher fields (ii) a non-monotonic temperature dependence of $κ_{xy}$ with a peak arising from the competition between thermal population and phonon scattering and (iii) strong enhancement of $κ_{xy}$ near the quantum critical point $ω_0 \to 0$, it exhibits power-law scaling $κ_{xy} \propto T^α$ with $α\approx 0.41$. Our findings provide an understanding of thermal Hall transport in quantum paraelectrics due to intrinsic paramagnetism and is aligned with the observed behaviour in SrTiO$_3$ and related materials.

papers.authors: Weiyan Qi, Stefano Ponzoni, Ashim Pramanik, Vitaly Gorelov, Yannis Laplace, Gianluca Stefanucci, Enrico Perfetto, Esteban Morcos, Marino Marsi, Steven Francis Udaundo, Sebastian Maherlein, Amina Taleb-Ibrahimi, Kaibo Zheng, Tonu Pullerits, Luca Perfetti

papers.abstract: Excitons are conventionally expected to destabilize at high photoexcitation densities, as screening weakens the electron-hole attraction. Recent studies, however, challenge this paradigm, suggesting that excitons generated by strong optical pumping can remain stable even beyond the onset of population inversion. Here, using time- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy on 2D hybrid perovskites, we provide direct evidence for such a high-density excitonic state, characterized by a distinctive Mexican-hat dispersion. Remarkably, this excitonic band reconstruction endures for orders of magnitude longer than the optical coherence time, revealing a population-sustained electronic structure that survives well into the incoherent regime. The excitonic resonance also persists far beyond optical saturation, at densities where exciton wavefunctions strongly overlap. Our findings reveal a long-lived, high-density quantum fluid of excitons with characteristics reminiscent of a BCS condensate, an electronic structure markedly different from that of the dilute limit.
papers.physics_advance: A Mexican-hat excitonic band reconstruction persists far beyond optical coherence and saturation, showing that a high-density excitonic state survives into the incoherent regime beyond the Mott limit.
papers.relevance_reason: Direct spectroscopic evidence for a persistent high-density excitonic electronic state is a substantial discovery about collective electronic matter in a solid.

papers.method_en: The study uses time- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy to examine the electronic structure of photoexcited 2D hybrid perovskites at high exciton densities.
papers.method_zh: 研究利用时间分辨角分辨光电子能谱，考察高激子密度下受光激发的二维杂化钙钛矿电子结构。
papers.result_en: The measurements identify a distinctive Mexican-hat dispersion associated with the high-density excitonic state, which persists for orders of magnitude longer than the optical coherence time. The excitonic resonance also remains beyond optical saturation, at densities where exciton wavefunctions strongly overlap, supporting a population-sustained electronic structure in the incoherent regime with characteristics reminiscent of a BCS condensate.
papers.result_zh: 测量发现与高密度激子态相关的独特墨西哥帽形色散，其存续时间比光学相干时间长多个数量级。激子共振在光学饱和之后仍然存在，此时激子波函数已强烈重叠；这支持一种由粒子占据维持、处于非相干区域的电子结构，其特征与 BCS 凝聚态有相似之处。
papers.future_en: Follow-up studies could map how the reconstructed dispersion and excitonic resonance depend on excitation density and time, and test how far the reported state can be distinguished from other high-density electronic regimes. Further characterization would also help establish the significance of the BCS-like analogy without presuming a coherent condensate.
papers.future_zh: 后续研究可测绘重构色散和激子共振随激发密度及时间的变化，并检验该态与其他高密度电子态之间的可区分程度。进一步表征也有助于界定其与 BCS 类比的意义，而不预先假定存在相干凝聚态。
papers.tier_reason_en: The abstract claims direct spectroscopic evidence for a long-lived, high-density excitonic electronic structure that survives far beyond optical coherence and saturation, challenging the conventional expectation of exciton destabilization at high density. The combination of a distinctive band reconstruction and persistence into the incoherent regime supports a high-impact physics or materials tier, although the abstract alone does not establish the full scope of validation.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 摘要声称以直接光谱证据揭示了一种长寿命高密度激子电子结构，其存续远超光学相干和饱和范围，挑战了高密度下激子失稳的传统预期。独特的能带重构与在非相干区域持续存在这两项结果，支持较高影响力的物理或材料期刊层级；不过，仅凭摘要无法判断完整验证的广度。

papers.title: Spontaneous Decay of High Energy Composite Fermions
papers.summary_en: The paper argues that a high-energy composite fermion with fractional charge can spontaneously decay into a collection containing quasiparticles, quasiholes, and whole electrons.
papers.summary: An electron, when added to a fractional quantum Hall fluid, famously splits into fractionally charged composite-fermion quasiparticles. We show here that a high energy composite fermion carrying a fractional charge decays into a collection of particles, including quasiparticles, quasiholes, and even whole electrons.
papers.abstract: An electron, when added to a fractional quantum Hall fluid, famously splits into fractionally charged composite-fermion quasiparticles. We show here that a high energy composite fermion carrying a fractional charge decays into a collection of particles, including quasiparticles, quasiholes, and even whole electrons.
papers.physics_advance: A high-energy fractionally charged composite fermion can spontaneously decay into a collection that includes quasiparticles, quasiholes, and whole electrons.
papers.relevance_reason: This is original theory of fractional quantum Hall quasiparticles and their decay, a direct contribution to correlated electronic matter.
papers.summary_zh: 本文指出，携带分数电荷的高能复合费米子可以自发衰变为由准粒子、准空穴乃至完整电子组成的粒子集合。
papers.method_en: The abstract states the proposed decay channels but does not specify the theoretical or experimental methods used to establish them.
papers.method_zh: 摘要说明了所提出的衰变通道，但未交代用于确立这些通道的理论或实验方法。
papers.result_en: The central result is that a high-energy composite fermion need not remain an intact fractional excitation; it can decay into multiple excitations, including whole electrons.
papers.result_zh: 核心结果是，高能复合费米子不必始终作为完整的分数激发存在；它可以衰变为多个激发，其中包括完整电子。
papers.future_en: A natural follow-up would be to determine the conditions governing the decay and the relative importance of its different final-state channels.
papers.future_zh: 一个自然的后续方向是确定该衰变发生的条件，以及不同末态通道的相对重要性。
papers.tier_reason_en: The abstract presents a conceptually interesting decay process in fractional quantum Hall physics, but gives no methodological details or quantitative evidence; on the available information, a specialist condensed-matter tier is the most proportionate assessment.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 摘要提出了分数量子霍尔物理中一个颇具概念意义的衰变过程，但未提供方法细节或定量证据；仅依据现有信息，凝聚态专业期刊档次较为相称。
